title: Delete the third copy of the config parser
action: D1 (store cd72ec97) exists because two parsers of one config shape had already drifted, and it says ONE parser owns the models.<runtime> shape. An audit found a THIRD live copy that no cell touched: normalize_models is re-implemented in verbs/status_full/store.rs around :465-494, hardcoding haiku, sonnet and opus as literals and keyed on a closed four-word list. Consequence, and this is a real user-visible bug rather than tidiness: bee status silently DROPS any role the operator configured outside those four words — so the operator who followed this feature's own advice and added models.claude.test sees nothing about it in status. The same file also hand-re-implements the review-inherits-generation fall-through in validate_agent_files_drift around :892-928, beside the AGENT_ROLES_BY_NAME table that already knows it. Collapse both onto the one parser in verbs/drivers. If status needs a different VIEW of the same data, that is a different function over one parse, not a second parse. Run your verify with --no-fail-fast.

truths: bee status shows a role the operator configured outside the historical four names
One parser owns the models.<runtime> shape; status_full holds no second copy
The review-inherits-generation rule is read from the shared table, not restated
No closed list of model names remains in status_full

trace.outcome: status reads the one models parser; the third copy and its closed four-slot list are gone
deviations: Widened scope to status_full/mod.rs (deleted MODEL_NORMALIZE_SLOTS and EFFORT_LEVELS, dead once the copy went) and status_full/tests.rs (3 regression tests); both reserved under mrs-w26 first.

Kept the opencode SEED in status: drivers::default_models leaves opencode null, but the drift check compares against agent files that pin AGENT_TIER_DEFAULTS_OPENCODE. It is a default, not a parser — same split onboard::agents already uses.

Behaviour improvement not named by the cell: a composite {primary,fallback_policy,fallback} slot now resolves to its primary model in the drift check. The old copy read .get("model") off the composite and reported a correctly-rendered file as stale.

Did not run a red-first demo of the bug: siblings mrs-w24/mrs-w25 are live in this worktree, so stashing to rebuild the old code was unsafe. The drop is a code-level fact — the old overlay walked MODEL_NORMALIZE_SLOTS and could not insert any other key.
